{{short description|Canadian mathematician}}
'''Melania Alvarez de Adem''' is a Mexican [[mathematics education|mathematics educator]] who works as the Education Coordinator at the [[Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences|Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences (PIMS)]], and Outreach Coordinator for the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of British Columbia]] in [[Vancouver]].

==Education==
Alvarez grew up in [[Mexico City]], where she completed her undergraduate education at the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]]. She later earned master's degrees in [[economics]] and [[anthropology]] from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] and in [[operations research]] from [[Stanford University]].{{r|gnm|pouliot}}
In 2016 she completed a Ph.D. in [[mathematics education]] at [[Simon Fraser University]] under the supervision of Peter Liljedahl.{{r|sfu}}

==Outreach==
Alvarez gained interest in helping disadvantaged minorities with mathematics from an incident of racial discrimination that occurred in [[Madison, Wisconsin|Madison]], where her sixth-grade son (who had inherited his mother's talent for mathematics) was placed in a lower-level mathematics track because of his Hispanic ethnicity. She moved to [[Vancouver]] in 2004, and began the PIMS Emerging Indigenous Scholars Summer School Program at [[University of British Columbia|UBC]] in 2007.{{r|gnm}}

At [[University of British Columbia|UBC]], Alvarez is known for the summer mathematics camps she developed to improve the mathematical education of [[Indigenous peoples in Canada|indigenous]] secondary-school students.{{r|gnm|tyee}} She is the 2012 winner of the [[Adrien Pouliot Award]], given by the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] for significant contributions to mathematics education in Canada.{{r|pouliot}}

As well as her work with indigenous people, Alvarez has been active in organizing mathematics competitions, workshops, and fundraising for mathematics education among the general population.{{r|pouliot|straight}}
